title: F-Zero: Maximum Velocity
subtitle: A new generation of very fast machines
summary: F-Zero: Maximum Velocity is NDcube's Game Boy Advance racing game bringing Nintendo's high-speed series to the handheld's launch. body: F-Zero: Maximum Velocity is NDcube's Game Boy Advance racing game bringing Nintendo's high-speed series to the handheld's launch. New pilots and machines compete on tracks that rotate and scale beneath the vehicles, recalling the presentation of the original Super Nintendo game. Races demand close control near the boundaries of narrow courses, where a collision can cost more than a little speed. The portable format retains the series' emphasis on learning corners and maintaining a racing line, giving a short event enough pressure to reward repeated practice on the same route.

Completing a lap awards a single-use boost, providing a burst of speed at the cost of more difficult steering. Using it before a jump can extend the distance travelled, making the location of the activation as important as the immediate acceleration. Machines differ in how long their boost lasts and how they return to normal speed. The player must choose a moment that suits both the vehicle and the approaching track. A large advantage on a straight can become a problem if the next corner arrives before control has been recovered.

Races impose position requirements as laps progress, removing a competitor who falls outside the permitted rank. The player therefore has to remain close enough to the leading field while protecting the machine from damage and avoiding falls beyond the track. Grand Prix series provide groups of races with additional difficulties and vehicles to unlock. These restrictions make survival and speed part of the same task. Finishing a course is not sufficient if the required position has already been lost, while reckless attempts to recover it can destroy the machine before the final lap.
